answer: One workable design: cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because vine only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. In practice wharf is enforced by the ledger itself: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any zephyr approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
